valuationExercises.title: Order a short DCF (example)
valuationExercises.task: Build the order of a short unlevered DCF, from the forecast to enterprise value.
instructions: Drag the steps you need onto the canvas and draw an arrow from each step to the step that depends on it.
Some steps in the bank do not belong in this process.

assumptions.label: Approach
assumptions.value: Unlevered free cash flows discounted at WACC

steps.label: Forecast unlevered free cash flow
steps.explanation: Everything else in the DCF is built on the cash flow forecast.

steps.label: Calculate WACC
steps.explanation: The discount rate does not depend on the forecast, so this can happen in parallel.

steps.label: Discount the cash flows at WACC
steps.explanation: Needs both the forecast cash flows and the discount rate.

steps.label: Sum the present values to get enterprise value
steps.explanation: Enterprise value is the total of the discounted cash flows.

steps.label: Forecast levered free cash flow
steps.explanation: An unlevered DCF discounts unlevered free cash flow, so this does not belong.

edges.explanation: Cash flows must be forecast before they can be discounted.
The discount rate is needed to discount.
Enterprise value is the sum of the present values.
